_comment: How research outputs are grouped and coloured in the two donut charts, on
One definition for both, so a slice is the same colour wherever it is drawn.
`types` are values of the `type` field in data/outputs.json.
Every type in data/outputs.json must be claimed by exactly one slice.
tools/build-cv.py enforces that and fails the build otherwise, which is what
keeps the chart total equal to the number of outputs there actually are —
add a new Zotero type here the day it first appears.
Why so few slices, when there are eleven output types: a donut is read by
matching any slice to any legend row, so every pair of colours has to be
tellable apart — under colour-vision deficiency, in light mode and dark.
Five hues is the most that clears that bar; the rest fold into one neutral.
The legend's count table carries the detail the wedges drop, and the
sections below the chart list every output individually.
Verified as a set, all-pairs, in both modes (worst normal-vision dE 17.2,
worst CVD dE 6.9, with the count table as the relief the two low-contrast
steps require). Do not substitute a colour without re-validating the whole
set — a hue that looks fine alone routinely collides with another one.
